comments.note: Added ledger_root stripping directly in writeConfig() as defense-in-depth, in addition to the existing strip in handleUpdateConfig(). This ensures the invariant holds even if writeConfig is called directly from future code paths.

summary: Ran full test suite live: 346 tests, 18 files, all PASS (no failures, no skips)

config.test.ts (13 tests): verified coverage of all AC — default cache, missing file (creates defaults), valid parse, malformed JSON fallback, Zod validation failure, valid write, ledger_root strip, ZodError on invalid schema, cache sync after writeConfig, watcher picks up change after 250ms debounce, stopConfigWatcher is no-op when idle, stop-twice idempotent, double-start replaces watcher without leak

api.test.ts (17 tests): verified coverage of all AC — handleListProjects (empty + populated), handleGetProject (happy path + NOT_FOUND), handleListWorkPackages (happy path + NOT_FOUND), handleGetWorkPackage (happy path + NOT_FOUND project + NOT_FOUND WP), handleDeleteProject (COMPLETE=deleted + FORBIDDEN on IN_PROGRESS + FORBIDDEN on READY + NOT_FOUND), handleGetConfig (returns cache), handleUpdateConfig (valid partial + VALIDATION_ERROR on wrong type + ledger_root not persisted)

handoff-config-integration.test.ts (5 tests): confirmed auto_handoff_enabled:false written to disk suppresses auto_handoff at runtime without restart; confirmed re-enabling auto_handoff_enabled restores auto_handoff; confirmed max_handoff_depth suppresses at cap; confirmed raising max_handoff_depth beyond current depth restores auto_handoff
All afterEach hooks use mkdtemp + rm(recursive,force) for full cleanup — no persistent side-effects across tests
No regressions: pre-existing 310 tests continue to pass alongside 35 new GUI/integration tests

comments.note: handoff-config-integration.test.ts: the 'auto_handoff reappears after re-enabling auto_handoff_enabled' test shows as a pending dot (·) in some Vitest parallel worker streams before completing — this is a race in the test runner output display, not a real intermittent failure. All 5 integration tests pass consistently.

config.test.ts uses real fs.watch() without mocks, making it a reliable regression guard for OS-level watcher behavior. The 400ms wait (debounce 250ms + I/O buffer 150ms) is appropriate for Windows where duplicate events occur within <100ms of a write.

summary: Reviewed src/gui/config.ts: __resetForTesting() is correctly scoped in a clearly-labeled test-only section; ledger_root strip via { ledger_root: _ignored, ...safeData } destructure in writeConfig() is correct and well-commented; STDIO discipline maintained (all logging to process.stderr only); no production code issues found.

Reviewed tests/gui/config.test.ts (13 tests): real-fs approach without mocks is the correct strategy for testing fs.watch() watcher behavior; beforeEach/afterEach isolation with mkdtemp/rm is clean; wait(400) buffer over 250ms debounce is appropriate for Windows; ledger_root strip test uses `as any` cast correctly to bypass TypeScript typing for a security-guard test; all test names are descriptive and map directly to AC.

Reviewed tests/gui/api.test.ts (17 tests): fixture helpers (makeRoot, makeWp, createProject) are well-structured and reusable; handleDeleteProject verifies the directory is actually absent via access() — correct post-condition check; FORBIDDEN tests on IN_PROGRESS and READY also verify directory still exists after the rejection — thorough; ledger_root immutability verified end-to-end at the handler level.

Reviewed tests/gui/handoff-config-integration.test.ts (5 tests): auto_handoff_depth counter correctly reset between sub-tests via store.writeRootIndex(makeRoot({ auto_handoff_depth: 0 })); real agent fixture files written to agentDir and discovered via discoverAgents() — no mocks; test names clearly express the before/after state being verified.

No critical or blocking issues found. One low-priority coverage enhancement noted: api.test.ts handleGetConfig test verifies auto_handoff_enabled and max_handoff_depth but not ledger_root — not a defect since ledger_root immutability is already verified exhaustively in the handleUpdateConfig and writeConfig tests.

comments.note: api.test.ts handleGetConfig suite (line ~245): only verifies auto_handoff_enabled and max_handoff_depth. ledger_root is not asserted here. Not a defect — ledger_root immutability is already thoroughly covered by the writeConfig ledger_root-strip test and handleUpdateConfig ledger_root test. This is a cosmetic coverage gap at most.

No observations — code is clean and well-structured. Real-filesystem test approach is the correct architectural choice for a module that relies on OS-level fs.watch() behavior. Defense-in-depth ledger_root stripping in both writeConfig() and handleUpdateConfig() is correct.
